review_notes: I read the whole file. I grepped Mathlib for PositiveDefinite and NegStar and found no matches, so Mathlib has no positive-definite-function predicate. I also grepped for `Star` instances defined as negation or inversion (patterns such as `star := Neg.neg`) under Mathlib and Mathlib/Algebra/Star. The only hits were the quaternion `star_eq_neg` lemmas, which are unrelated. So `WithNegStar` does not compete with an existing synonym. `IsPositiveDefiniteSub` is a documented specialisation of the library's own generic `IsPositiveDefinite` for the negation involution, and `isPositiveDefiniteSub_iff_isPositiveDefinite` transports results between the two. The file explains why the separate predicate exists: Mathlib's `star` on real vector spaces is the identity. The `Matrix.PosSemidef` characterisation reuses the existing Mathlib notion. Within TauCeti I saw no second competing definition of the subtraction-form predicate, only uses of it. I did not read every use site. The residual uncertainty is whether the many thin transfer lemmas could be consolidated. That is wrapper-API design, which the rubric does not treat as a defect.
